title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure

definitions.HFrEF: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: LVEF ≤40%
definitions.HFmrEF: Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction: LVEF 41–49%
definitions.HFpEF: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: LVEF ≥50%
definitions.NYHA Class I: No symptoms with ordinary physical activity
definitions.NYHA Class II: Slight limitation; comfortable at rest, symptoms with moderate exertion
definitions.NYHA Class III: Marked limitation; comfortable at rest, symptoms with minimal exertion
definitions.NYHA Class IV: Symptoms at rest or with any physical activity
definitions.Stage A: At risk for HF, no structural heart disease or symptoms
definitions.Stage B: Pre-HF: structural/functional cardiac changes, no symptoms

recommendations.text: For patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), ACEi or ARB or ARNI therapy is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality.
Evidence-based beta blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol) are recommended for all stable patients with HFrEF to reduce mortality.
MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone) is recommended for patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤35%) and NYHA Class II–IV to reduce mortality and hospitalizations.
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) are recommended in patients with HFrEF to reduce HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality.
In patients with HFrEF tolerating an ACEi or ARB, replacement with sacubitril/valsartan is recommended to further reduce morbidity and mortality.
Diuretics are recommended in patients with HF and fluid retention to improve symptoms.
ICD therapy is recommended in selected patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤35%) with NYHA Class II–III on GDMT to reduce sudden cardiac death.
CRT is indicated for patients with LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with QRS ≥150 ms, and NYHA Class II–IV on GDMT.
SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended in patients with HFpEF to decrease hospitalizations for HF and cardiovascular mortality.
Routine use of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids may be considered in patients with HF to reduce CV mortality and HF hospitalizations.
Calcium channel blockers with negative inotropic effects (diltiazem, verapamil) are potentially harmful in HFrEF.
ARNI should not be administered concomitantly with or within 36 hours of ACE inhibitors.
Hydralazine-nitrate combination is recommended for patients who identify as Black/African American with NYHA Class III–IV HFrEF on GDMT to reduce morbidity and mortality.
Ivabradine is recommended to reduce HF hospitalisations in stable patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤35%), sinus rhythm, resting HR ≥70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta-blocker.
Coronary revascularization is reasonable in selected patients with HFrEF and significant CAD who have viable myocardium.
